correctness.rationale: From the source-given survival S(x)=e exp(-exp((tau*x)^eta)) exp(-(kappa*x)^phi), the nonnegative-variable moment formula r∫x^(r-1)S(x)dx is finite for every positive integer r by exp[-(kappa*x)^phi] domination. Substitution in the published Eq.(3.2) coefficient yields at all-one parameters a_(i,j)=e(-1)^i i^j/i! and hence exactly a_(1,j)=-e for every j. This fixed-row term test refutes convergence, a fortiori absolute double convergence, without any truncation. Substitution z=exp((tau*x)^p) yields r e/(p tau^r)∫_1^∞ (log z)^(r/p-1)z^(-c-1)e^(-z)dz with c=(kappa/tau)^p. At r=p this is e tau^(-p)Gamma(-c,1); mpmath quadrature independently equals e Gamma(-1,1)≈0.4036526376768059 at the all-one point and verifies a second shape slice. This does not imply the distribution lacks moments or all related series are invalid.
